title: enterprise-probe-workbook-llm-signal-variance-and-leakage-sampler
creator: Maya Lin
description: Goal: build a repeatable probe workbook and telemetry pipeline to quantify substitution risk, signal leakage, and service-level drift for enterprise LLM customers. We need an experiment catalog + lightweight instrumentation that lets PMs and SREs run probes (synthetic + sampled production subsets) to measure: performance delta between model variants, cost per productive token, fidelity degradation on representative enterprise prompts, and early warning signals that predict customer-visible regressions. Deliverables include an experiment matrix, a data contract for telemetry events, a dashboard template, automated alert recipes, and a triage playbook for actioning signals.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry schema (event names/fields) published and agreed with Eng: includes model_variant, model_commit, prompt_signature, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, rerank_score, error_code, sample_id
Dashboard template in Console (telemetry view) that shows time-series for variant delta: median latency, 95p latency, cost per effective response, and fidelity regressions by prompt cohort
Experiment catalog with 12 prioritized probes (3 enterprise verticals x 4 probe types) and run instructions
Automated alert recipes: (1) sustained >15% increase in cost_per_response for critical cohort, (2) >10% drop in fidelity on regression prompt-set across 3 consecutive runs
Playbook documented with triage steps, rollback criteria, and example GitHub PR and rollback commands
tasks: Define representative enterprise prompt cohorts (legal-docs, support-concise, long-context-RAG)
Work with Eng to add new telemetry event fields and sampling flags
Create synthetic probe generator (small harness repo) and sample-run harness for production subsets
Design dashboard panels and set baseline thresholds from historical runs
Coordinate a 2-week pilot with 2 internal customers (AE sandbox + Platform QA)
notes: Reasoning: Sales and Customer Success often ask for quantitative evidence when proposing model switches or reserved capacity changes. We lack a lightweight, standardized way to demonstrate substitution risk for a given customer workload.
Trade-offs considered: full-fidelity A/B tests on production traffic are ideal but costly and high-risk; this project favors sampled production + synthetic probes to balance speed vs. risk.
